question.prompt:
All of the triangles in the diagram below are similar to isosceles triangle \(ABC,\) in which \(AB = AC.\) Each of the \(7\) smallest triangles has area \(1,\) and \(\triangle ABC\) has area \(40.\) What is the area of trapezoid \(DBCE?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2018_AMC_12A_Q08_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
[Figure 1](figures/2018_AMC_12A_Q08_question_fig1.svg)

The seven small triangles lie between the same two lines. Establishing that these lines are parallel will let us compare their bases using their equal areas.

Let \(F\) and \(G\) be the endpoints of the upper interior segment, on \(AB\) and \(AC\), respectively. By the given similarity and the common angle at \(A\), \(\triangle AFG\) is isosceles with \(AF=AG\). Its base angles equal those of \(\triangle ABC\), so \(FG\parallel BC\). Also, \(DE\parallel BC\) because these are the parallel sides of trapezoid \(DBCE\). Hence \(FG\parallel DE\).

Let \(t>0\) be the distance between \(FG\) and \(DE\). Each small triangle has height \(t\) when its side on one of these lines is used as its base. Since each has area \(1\), all these bases have the same length \(b\), with
\[
\frac12 bt=1.
\]
Four such base segments partition \(DE\), while three partition \(FG\). Therefore \(DE=4b\) and \(FG=3b\).

Let \(H\) be the height of \(\triangle ADE\) to \(DE\). The height of \(\triangle AFG\) is \(H-t\). Similarity makes corresponding heights proportional to bases, giving
\[
\frac{H-t}{H}=\frac{3b}{4b}=\frac34,
\qquad H=4t.
\]
Consequently,
\[
[ ADE ]=\frac12(4b)(4t)
=16\left(\frac12 bt\right)=16.
\]
Here brackets denote area. Removing this upper triangle from \(\triangle ABC\) leaves the requested trapezoid, whose area is
\[
[DBCE]=40-16=\boxed{24},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Use the common height of the small triangles
